candidates.detail: The party-join acceptance reducer snapshots every source party inventory row. For an item whose catalog projection is not repairable, it grants the target party entry.quantity of that item and deletes the source row, without selecting the existing stable object, amount or food lot. Food is a measured, stable-object item, so the checked grant for a positive quantity creates a new quantity-one row, new object, whole amount and fresh catalog-derived FoodLot and contamination state. This happens even if the grant succeeds; error erasure is a separate connected concern. Under an authorized otherwise-successful merge with one source travel_ration row whose amount and food lot have been partly consumed, the destination row is initialized as a full catalog ration rather than receiving the original remainder. The pinned SpacetimeDB dependency documents that a successful reducer commits; actual transaction and user-visible behavior were not executed.
candidates.source_derived_example: The authored travel_ration has 2,500 kcal and no durability capability, so its projected Item is non-repairable. The party travel-food consumer retains the same quantity-one row when partially consumed and scales its FoodLot material and PartyItemAmount. Assuming a valid source lot with 1,250 kcal and half its material remaining, a later successful qualifying party merge calls the new-item grant with quantity one: that source path initializes a whole amount and a 2,500-kcal lot. The original age, food-lot identity, preparation, ingredient and contamination provenance are not transferred to that new lot. The exact admitted sequence, resulting database rows and any observed player impact remain unverified.
